Branch: `feat/bm_readiness`
Scope: `simulation/server/pattern_manifest.cjs`, `marsin_engine/patterns/manifest.json`
(generator output only), `simulation/tests/pattern_manifest.test.js`, `launcher.js`,

## 1. What the three reds actually were

`_233` §5 flagged three `pattern_manifest.test.js` failures left by the
pattern-curation wave rewriting the tree at 01:57. Re-verified before touching
anything — all three still stood, and one of them was the reverse of what the
name suggests.

| Red | What it actually was |
|---|---|
| `patterns/ambient_extra/ is neither registered nor excluded` | A new family on disk (`01_harbor_glass`, `02_brass_compass`), unclassified. **This is the urgent one**: `listPatterns` throws on an unclassified directory, so it also failed the *round-trip* test — and it is the same throw the save server would hit at the next `npm start`. |
| `baby/ is not fully registered in the manifest` | **29 new files on disk that the tracked JSON never learned about** — `baby/52_boy_bow_wave` … `baby/80_girl_celebration_bloom`. The manifest stopped at `baby/51`. Not a registry bug: the registry already had `baby`, the checked-in JSON was simply stale against the tree. |
| the generated `default.yaml` set | **Rot was REPAIRED, not spread.** The pin expected `['studio', 'summer_camp_dome', 'titanic']`; reality was `['studio', 'summer_camp_dome']`. `titanic/default.yaml` was regenerated by the curation session and its rot — the three deleted root `13x_baby_*` ids — went with it. All 27 of its entries now resolve. |

That last one is worth stating plainly, because the assertion message says *"do
not widen this list"*: the list did not widen, it **narrowed**, and the honest
move was to follow the data down. Widening is the direction that hides a
regression; narrowing records one that was fixed. The `studio` and
`summer_camp_dome` copies still name the 45 pre-move unqualified
`patterns/summer_camp/` ids and stay pinned exactly as they were.

## 2. The classification call — `ambient_extra` is REGISTERED

Inclusive default, per the brief. Both files are full show patterns with
instrument staging for BARs, RAW LED, VINTAGE heads, PARs and both TE signs;
both carry a `// DRAFT — pending operator review` first line.

The asymmetry decides it: a draft that is visible in the operator's pattern
picker costs a picker row, while a finished pattern that is invisible costs the
show the pattern — and nothing announces the second failure. So it goes in
`MANIFEST_PATTERN_DIRS`, with the reverse move written down at the definition:

```js
// `ambient_extra` is registered on the INCLUSIVE default: it holds full show
// patterns (currently headed "DRAFT — pending operator review") … If the family
// turns out to be scratch, the reversible call is to move the name into
// NON_MANIFEST_PATTERN_DIRS below with its reason — nothing else changes.
```

One line, one direction, no data migration either way — the manifest is
regenerated from the registry, so flipping the classification is the entire
edit. If the curation session disagrees, that is the change to make.

## 3. The manifest, regenerated

Through `listPatterns()` itself, written exactly as `save-server.js`
`writePatternManifest()` writes it (`JSON.stringify(…, null, 2) + '\n'`), so the
tracked file is byte-identical to what the next sim boot produces:

```
before 140 → after 171
ADDED (31): ambient_extra/01_harbor_glass, ambient_extra/02_brass_compass,
            baby/52_boy_bow_wave … baby/80_girl_celebration_bloom
REMOVED (0)
```

Zero removals matters in a shared tree: the regeneration could not have dropped
anything the curation session had just added.

## 4. One fixture change the registry forced

`an unclassified pattern subdirectory fails loudly instead of vanishing`
went red *after* the registry edit — its sandbox created `baby/` and
`party_dancers/` by hand, and the other half of the policy ("a registered
directory that is missing is a throw") correctly fired on the absent
`ambient_extra/`. The fixture now builds its tree **from
`MANIFEST_PATTERN_DIRS`**, so registering the next family cannot break the test
that guards registration. The contract under test is untouched: the sandbox
still asserts the clean generation and still asserts the unclassified-family
throw by name.

## 5. `launcher.js --force-sacn`

`_233` §4 shipped the arm interlock with two override spellings and noted the
flag could not reach `launcher.js`, which exits 2 on an unknown option.

The mechanism turns out to need **acceptance, not forwarding**: `launcher.js`
`require`s `tools/port_cleanup.cjs` **in-process**, and `forceSacnKillRequested()`
reads `process.argv` — the launcher's own. So the flag already arrives; the
parser was simply killing the invocation before any port work began. One case:

```js
case portCleanup.FORCE_SACN_KILL_FLAG: break;
```

matched off the shared constant rather than re-spelled, with the reason in a
comment, plus three `--help` lines that say what the override *costs* (every
mirrored box freezes on its last frame) and name the env var equivalent.
Verified: `node launcher.js --force-sacn --help` → usage, exit **0**.

Two now-stale claims were corrected with it: the `forceSacnKillRequested()`
doc comment in `port_cleanup.cjs` and the explanatory comment in
`port_cleanup_arm_interlock.test.js`, both of which still said the launcher
rejects the flag.

## 6. Verification

`cd simulation && node --test tests/*.test.js`

| | tests | pass | fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_233` after | 2305 | 2293 | 11 |
| `_234` after | 2306 | 2298 | **7** |

The +1 test is a source pin (`_234: launcher.js ACCEPTS the flag instead of
exiting 2 on it`) in `port_cleanup_arm_interlock.test.js` — it reads
`launcher.js` and requires both the constant-matched `case` and the constant's
appearance in `--help`, because an override nobody can find is not an override.

**The failing list is the `_227` group, exactly, and nothing else:**

```
✖ CLI: --require-applied fails (exit 3) while Phase B has not applied the block
✖ CLI: default emit against the real scenes exits 0 and reports parity=absent
✖ Live display orientation is a pure projection of authoritative 3D coordinates
✖ REFUSES: a patched fixture no chain reaches (orphan patch record)
✖ _176 §5.3: a TEST-CONTEXT write into the REPO's real scenes dir is REFUSED
✖ fixtures are docked beside the ship, not left inside the hull
✖ the real titanic scene can accept the block today (no collisions)
```

7, not the 8 `_233` recorded. The eighth was `_233`'s "playlist red" — and the
only playlist-named test in the whole sim suite is
`every curated playlist entry in every scene names a registered pattern`, i.e.
the `default.yaml` assertion in this very file, which `_233`'s baseline run
caught mid-rewrite. It is green now. All 6 `pattern_manifest.test.js` tests and
all 20 `port_cleanup_arm_interlock.test.js` tests pass.

**No test residue.** `git status --porcelain` diffed across the suite run: the
sole delta is another session's `20260815_231_wedding_show.md` appearing. No
writes to `simulation/scenes/**` or `marsin_engine/states/**`, and
